messages:
maya: Heads-up — the raven-int4 canary we spun up overnight is showing a concentrated spike of funcall parse failures (struct output non-compliance). ETA: started ~03:20 UTC.

sam: ugh. numbers? where do they come from (streaming vs non-streaming)?

maya: Canary-bot summary pasted below from the run:
canary-bot: canary run id=run-2026-03-21-03:20, model=raven-int4, total_invokes=18,742, parse_failures=412 (2.2%), malformed_json=298, truncated_stream=94, nonjson-suffix=20

liam: 2.2% is high for funcalls. is this correlated with high token lengths / long kvcache prefixes?

maya: quick sample of failing output (redacted prompt):
```json
Expected schema: {"action": "string", "args": {"item_id": "string", "qty": integer}}
\nActual model chunked stream (joined):
{"action": "create_order", "args": {"item_id": "sku-123", "qty": 3,}}
```
Note the trailing comma and then a truncated eos in a number of streams where the model sends a control char and we end up with a broken parse. Also some streaming fragments show split arrays like "args": {"items": [\n{"id": "a"` then stream ends and next chunk starts with `, "qty": 1}` which confuses our NDJSON rejoin heuristics.

ana: hypothesis: quantization (int4) changed tokenization/emission patterns causing more control chars and earlier eos. Could also be KV prefix length shifting chunk boundaries.

sam: agree. two quick probes: 1) run same canary on raven-int8 with identical prompts and compare parse-fail rate; 2) re-run raven-int4 canary with kvcache disabled to see if prefix-induced splits are main factor.

liam: also let's try running the postprocess json-sanitizer rule before parse (strip trailing commas, remove control chars, balanced-brace heuristics). That might reduce noise and buy us time. But we need to know if this is masking a regression vs the model actually changing behavior.

maya: TL;DR action plan proposal:
- A: run raven-int8 canary (same seed set) -> compare rates (sam)
- B: run raven-int4 canary with kvcache off -> compare rates (liam)
- C: enable json-sanitizer in probe pipeline for 1k samples and record how many parse_failures would be recovered (ana)
- D: collect top 50 failing prompts and see when failures started (time-based drift) (maya)

ana: for (C) can we use the existing sanitizer rules? snippet: 
```js
function sanitize(s) {
  // remove common control chars
  s = s.replace(/[\u0000-\u001F]/g, '');
  // fix trailing commas in objects/arrays
  s = s.replace(/,\s*([}\]])/g, '$1');
  return s;
}
```
We should log whether sanitizer changed semantics (e.g., removed meaningful control chars).

sam: metrics probe: add parse_error_type dimension (trailing_comma, truncated_stream, nonjson_suffix, encoding_controlchar). Also track prefix_length and first_k_tokens.

liam: small experiment: on a 5k-sample subset, run 3 variants in parallel: int4 with sanitizer, int4 without, int8 without sanitizer. Keep identical prompts and seeds. compare token-level emission diffs and parse failure counts. If int8 much better -> quantization-induced spike.

maya: I ran a quick 500-sample pilot last hour: raven-int8 parse_fail=1.0%, raven-int4 parse_fail=2.4%, raven-int4+sanitizer recovered 0.9% (net parse_fail ~1.5%). So sanitizer recovers a good chunk but not all.

ana: that suggests both quantization emission quirks and some streaming boundary issues. We should also look at where KV prefix length is >512 tokens in failing cases.

sam: canary config tweak: add `--log-prefix-len` and `--emit-chunk-boundaries` flags so we capture exact chunk split points for each failing invoke. That will help tell if a structural token boundary aligns with JSON bracket boundaries.

maya: I'm worried about masking a regression with sanitizer. We need to ship a short-term fallback (sanitizer + retry) but also a rollback/mitigation plan if int4 causes customer-visible issues.

liam: propose: implement sanitizer + one automatic retry with slight temperature drop and `max_new_tokens=0` (regen suffix only) on parse_failures labeled `truncated_stream` or `trailing_comma`. If that succeeds, count as auto-heal and surface in telemetry. If not, fallback to int8 route for that customer session.

ana: testing note: ensure the retry budget/latency SLO isn't blown. Measure median extra latency for auto-retries. We can gate this behavior behind feature flags per-customer.

sam: I'll own the int8 vs int4 canary runs. Liam, you own kvcache-off experiment and chunk-boundary logging. Ana, run sanitizer recovery eval and collect top-50 failing prompts. Maya will do drift analysis and coordinate rollout decisions.

maya: thanks — I'll post a short PR template for the canary re-runs (commands + dataset ids). Quick command to start a canary run we used: 
```bash
./tools/run_canary --id run-2026-03-21-03:20 --model raven-int4 --prompts dataset://funcall-canary-v2 --samples 5000 --emit-chunk-boundaries
```

liam: added to my queue. ping me if you want pre-built debug images with extra logging.

ana: one more ask: collect token-level diffs for 200 recovered cases (int4 vs int8) so we can feed to research for a micro-batch quantization behavior review.

maya: noted. I'll create the tracking ticket and drop links here once done.

sam: :thumbsup:

liam: assigning labels: severity=medium, dst=canary, owner=eng-ml-triage. I'll update the run when complete.

maya: cool. will follow up with results tomorrow morning. Thanks everyone.
